No directly matched controlled study surfaced comparing randomly initialized, jointly trained mean-pooling versus order-sensitive title/description encoders in sequential recommendation on these specific distinctions. [Deep Averaging Networks](https://aclanthology.org/P15-1162/) show that unordered representations can compete on text classification; this does not establish product-compatibility understanding or transfer to the no-pretraining setting. Architectural inference: averaging context-independent token embeddings is permutation invariant, so “HDMI to VGA” and “VGA to HDMI” collide when token multisets match. Model numbers and media-format tokens can remain distinguishable if tokenization preserves them; dimensions lose axis assignments when values are permuted. CNNs, RNNs or position-aware Transformers can represent these distinctions, but recommendation supervision may not teach them.

Recommended controlled ablation: retain the HSTU backbone, tokenizer, training data, seeds and budget; compare mean pooling with a small order-sensitive encoder, training each separately without score fusion. Test token shuffling and minimal text pairs that reverse connector direction, swap dimension assignments, or replace one model-number/format token. Measure representation changes and candidate-score changes separately: sensitivity alone does not establish correctness. [Conneau et al.’s probing study](https://aclanthology.org/P18-1198/) supplies established word-content and adjacent-word-swap diagnostics; product-specific adaptations remain proposed checks.

For shortcuts, mask title-derived brand strings, retain brand strings alone, remove generic product words, and retain only model/connector/dimension/format spans. Combine inference-time perturbations with retrained ablations to distinguish reliance from corruption sensitivity. Examine naturally occurring same-brand, high-title-overlap candidates differing in critical specifications. Report these as auxiliary validation diagnostics while preserving the pinned evaluator and macro HR@10; use only supplied titles/descriptions, not unavailable brand metadata.
